messages:
maya: heads-up — around 03:40 UTC we saw a sharp p95 regression on /v1/generate. users saw multi-second responses (~1.8s). graphs show a burst of scale activity at the same time.
leo: grabbing traces now. initial look: high KV cache miss rate and several kernel selection fallbacks. also saw longer batch head waits.
infra-bot: autoscaler_event: {event: "scale_up", pool: "dedicated-gpu-b", requested: 4, launched: 1, queued: 3, ts: 1790023456}
sam: can you paste the profiler excerpt? curious if the fallback to slower GEMM kernels is frequent.
maya: profiler snippet from trace-8a1c:
```
[trace-8a1c] token0 -> kernel=fast-gemm
kernel_exec: 180ms
KV cache miss rate: 72%
batching wait p95: 410ms headwait: 520ms
fallback_count: 4 (to slow-gemm)
```
leo: KV miss spike looks like it coincided with an on-host memory reclaim. node kubelet logged evictions and a couple container restarts. noisy neighbor GPU load likely triggered reclaim.
ida: kube events show "Pending handoff" for new pods with average wait 0.6-1.1s while provisioner assigned resources.
sam: so chain is noisy node -> reclaim -> KV eviction + restarts -> autoscaler spins up pods -> handoff queue + coldstart -> kernel fallback + longer batching wait = amplified p95.
maya: autoscaler log segment:
```
[autoscaler] desired=7 current=2
[autoscaler] enqueue: 5 pods
[provisioner] handoff_queue len=5 avg_wait=0.79s
[provisioner] launched: 1 of 5
```
leo: note: yesterday's batching heuristic change increased max_wait_ms for small flows to 30ms. that made initial head-of-line blocking worse during warmup.
ida: plus, KV prefetch was turned off in this cluster as an experiment, so every new replica had to fetch large prefix on startup which increased contention and kernel setup cost.
maya: incident summary: noisy neighbor triggered host reclaim -> widespread KV evictions and a few container restarts -> autoscaler created new replicas -> provisioner handoff queue added ~0.6–1.2s per pod -> replicas started cold -> kernel fallback + increased batch waits -> p95 spike.
ops-bot: created INC-2026-81 severity: high-latency
sam: mitigations we rolled out within ~10m:
- rolled back batching heuristic (reverted deploy 2026-03-15T22:03)
- pinned model family to stable kernel path (disabled fallback for the affected model temporarily)
- increased warm pool min_replicas from 1 -> 4 for the shard
- re-enabled KV prefetch in the cluster canary
maya: quick metrics after mitigations (03:50): p95 dropped to ~310ms, KV miss rate down to ~20% within 3mins, warm pool filled.
leo: action items / follow-ups:
- PERF-421: investigate provisioner handoff locking and rate limiting to reduce queue time (I'll own)
- PERF-422: measure KV prefetch startup cost vs network IO in canary and roll plan
- SRE-230: noisy-node postmortem with node telemetry and cloud provider (ida owns)
- Add guardrail: if handoff_queue > 2 then preemptively grow warm pool during decision window
sam: also adding an alert for provisioner handoff avg_wait p95 > 500ms and tie that into on-call runbook.
maya: flagged CS for customers on Dedicated who may have seen SLA degradation.
ops-bot: incident status: mitigated (03:52), watch until 04:30
maya: thanks all — I'll post a short postmortem draft in #postmortems once we have flamegraphs attached. please append any additional logs to INC-2026-81.
